person.persName: الجويني, ابو المعالي عبد الملك بن ابي محمد عبد الله بن يوسف
al-Ǧuwaynī, Abū al-Maʻālī ʻAbd al-Malik b. Abī Muḥammad ʻAbd Allāh b. Yūsuf
person.floruit: 5th / 9th century (d. 478 / 1085)He was connected with the school of ʿilm al-kalām inaugurated by Abū al-Ḥasan al-Ašʿarī at the beginning of the 4th/10th century. But ʿAmīd al-Mulk al-Kundurī, vizier of the Salǧūq Tuġrul Beg, declared himself against this “innovation”, and had the Ašʿarīs, as well as the Rawāfiḍ, denounced from the pulpits. Al-Ǧuwaynī, like Abū al-Qāsim al-Qušayrī, immediately left his country and went to Baġdād; then, in 450/1058, he reached the Ḥiǧāz where he taught at Mecca and at Medina for four years: hence his honorary name of “Imām of the two holy Cities”. But when the vizier Niẓām al-Mulk came to power in the Salǧūq empire, he favoured the Ašʿarīs and invited the emigrants to return home.
person.death: 1085-08-20 The date of death in the article of the Encyclopaedia of Islam does not coincide.
